correctness.rationale: PASS: In the cube Q=[-1,1]^n, the exit distance in direction v is 2S_v, S_v=min_i U_i/|v_i|, where U_i are independent Uniform[0,1]. Its survival probability P(S>t)=∏(1-|v_i|t) on [0,1/max|v_i|] yields the precise finite elementary-symmetric formula for the radial-p gauge for every finite p>-1; the logarithmic p=0 limit is separate. At any zero coordinate, differentiating with respect to its absolute value gives a strictly positive axial derivative and opposite signed one-sided slopes. In an orthant and at an m-fold maximal tie, freezing the endpoint changes an interval of length O(δ) on which all m competing factors are O(δ); this gives a uniform O(δ^{m+1}) difference from an analytic continuation and hence a Peano m-jet. The one-coordinate right perturbation gives the nonzero negative (m+1)-order coefficient -a^{-p-m-1}∏_{j>m}(1-b_j/a)/[m(m+1) M_p], with no counterpart on the left. Matched second derivatives across finitely many analytic cells and bounded one-sided third derivatives yield local C^{2,1}, but generic m=2 ties preclude C³. Affine covariance follows from exit distances. The finite bundled arithmetic code was inspected; its samples are not treated as a proof.

evidence: Langharst Theorem 2 gives convexity of R_pK for every convex K and every p>-1, but makes no C²/C³ claim for cube gauges.
Proposition 34 gives n-dimensional cube radial integral and axial/diagonal values, not the Peano jet multiplicity transition.

value.rationale: PASS: Radial mean body regularity at coordinate-zero seams and multiple-max ties is a natural precise geometry question. The theorem gives a complete affine-invariant stratification, identifies the exact first forbidden jet order at every multiplicity, and separates pointwise higher jets from neighborhood smoothness. It goes beyond a routine substitution into the known integral representation.

limitations: Restricted to n≥3, finite p>-1, open orthants and affine parallelotopes, excluding p=∞ and general convex bodies.
Numerical checks do not certify every parameter; analytic boundary-layer and finite-cell gluing supply the proof.
